title: Consolidate client SDK dependencies and clean deprecated API endpoints
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Over the last 18 months we've accumulated multiple divergent dependency versions across our official SDKs and retained a handful of legacy API surface paths (legacy/generate, legacy/embeddings) that complicate routing, telemetry, and client footprint. This ticket consolidates dependency bumps across Python, JS/TS, and Go SDKs and removes the last compatibility-only code paths for the v0 legacy endpoints. Goal: reduce transitive vulnerability exposure, shrink SDK bundle sizes, align on a single supported set of runtime versions, and remove internal conditionals that add latency and maintenance burden. This is a cross-language, low-risk refactor with a migration window and compatibility shims during rollout.
acceptance_criteria:
1) All three SDKs (python, javascript/typescript, go) pass the full SDK integration test matrix on Node 18+, Python 3.10+, Go 1.20+ after dependency upgrades.
2) All deprecated endpoints are behind a feature-flag and return a structured deprecation warning in responses when enabled.
3) Feature-flag disabled: legacy endpoints return 410 and guidance header with migration link.
4) No new high/critical OSS vulnerabilities introduced (Snyk/Dependabot reports green).
5) CI artifacts (wheel, npm tarball, go module) bundle size reduced or unchanged vs baseline.
6) Migration guide and changelog entries published and linked in SDK repos and docs site.
implementation_notes:
High level plan: 
- Create a single dev branch per SDK (sdk/deps/consolidate) and open coordinated PRs.
- Python: move to httpx>=0.24, drop urllib3 pin, bump mypy/typing deps, replace legacy backoff util with retrying from internal rpc library. Update setup metadata to declare Python 3.10+ and build manylinux2014 wheels.
- JS/TS: bump typescript to >=5.2, node-target to 18, update bundled ESM/CJS build steps, replace deprecated Qs dependency with url-search-params helper, migrate to undici for HTTP runtime.
- Go: tidy go.mod, bump to go1.20 target, replace internal http client wrapper with net/http + context improvements, remove shim for old token format.
- Introduce a server-side feature flag 'legacy_api_compat' to gate legacy endpoints during rollout. When enabled, responses include 'X-Redwood-Deprecation' header with migration URL.
- Add automated migration tests that assert deprecation header, 410 behavior, and client compatibility.
- Run vulnerability scan and bundle analysis before merge.
- Coordinate release notes and staged release (canary NPM, PyPI pre-release, go module tag).
rollout_plan:
1) Week 1: Open PRs and run CI; internal dogfood on staging with feature flag ON.
2) Week 2: Address review feedback, security scans, and performance microbenchmarks.
3) Week 3: Canary release to select customers and partner apps; monitor telemetry for errors, latency regressions, and error rates.
4) Week 4: Toggle feature flag OFF on production (legacy endpoints return 410) and publish migration guide.
5) Post-release: 2-week observation window with automated rollback plan if customer impact > medium.
risks:
- Some customers still use legacy endpoints. Mitigation: staged flag, clear header + migration docs, Support/CS holding migration list.
- Behavior drift due to different HTTP client (undici/httpx) subtle buffering differences. Mitigation: extensive integration tests and request/response snapshot tests.
- Third-party transitive vulnerabilities introduced by new deps. Mitigation: pre-merge SCA, pin known-good versions, security review.
- Build/tooling failures for older CI images. Mitigation: ensure CI images include required runtimes and add matrix for minimal supported versions.
